A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ImDy dataset and ImDyS solver. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including v2's added Appendices C–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on ImDy, GroundLink, and AddBiomechanics, along with ablations, application examples, and appendix analyses of prediction failures and data quality.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds fine-tuning comparisons, forward-dynamics evaluation, original-PHC results, and an ImDy activity-distribution analysis.

M1.justification: The data-collection procedure, marker-based transformer, prediction heads, losses, and two-stage training remain unchanged. Appendix D explains the existing loss data flow; the model without fine-tuning is an experimental ablation.

E1.justification: The named benchmarks and data sizes remain stable, and the added analyses examine existing data and model functions. However, Section 3.2 changes KIT's source citation from Mandery et al. (2016) to Krebs et al. (2021), whose reference describes a bimanual manipulation dataset. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects attribution or changes the underlying motion source.

E2.justification: Appendix F adds the original PHC to the GroundLink comparison, alongside the retained retrained PHC. Table 8 adds Nimble as an evaluated forward-dynamics comparator; v1 only discussed it as prior work. Existing benchmark comparators remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation procedures compare knee-torque magnitudes with and without sim-to-real fine-tuning and measure forward-dynamics marker RMSE on the AddBiomechanics test set. The existing splits, resampling, training budgets, and main evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic coverage beyond the retained representation, loss, window-size, and data-quality analyses. Appendix C isolates fine-tuning effects; Appendix E evaluates the auxiliary forward-dynamics model; Appendix F examines whether PHC jitter persists with the original controller. Figure 12 additionally compares ImDy and AddBiomechanics activity distributions using BABEL annotations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its evaluations. The added results continue the existing point-estimate and qualitative reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their values. New Table 8 reports RMSEs of 0.0302, 0.0194, and 0.0186 for the baseline, ImDyS, and Nimble. Appendix F adds original-PHC left/right-foot errors of 1.559/3.518. Figure 15 shows oversized, overactive torques without fine-tuning, and Figure 12 adds ImDy's activity distribution. These supplement rather than revise the existing benchmark results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the mathematical formulation are retained. Appendix D restates the existing forward-dynamics consistency loss using an intermediate predicted-state symbol; it introduces no new derivation, formal assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: scalable imitation-based dynamics collection, the ImDyS solver, and effectiveness on simulated and real-world data. The appendix additions support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix C narrows direct cross-model torque comparison to approximately corresponding knees and proposes mass, inertia, and degrees-of-freedom differences as explanations for excessive unfine-tuned torques. Appendix F suggests imperfect contact simulation contributes to PHC jitter. These refine v1's existing sim-to-real discussion and limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix D and Figure 16 make the prior and forward-dynamics data flow more explicit, while Figure 12 identifies BABEL as the activity-annotation source. The KIT source citation is revised. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training-time disclosure, and project link remain unchanged; no implementation change is established.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting robotics, healthcare, sports, and motion-generation applications, plus Krebs et al. (2021) for KIT. The AddBiomechanics publication update refers to the same work. The central positioning of imitation learning as a source of inverse-dynamics knowledge remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives localized wording edits, updated affiliations and publication headers, and acknowledgements. Appendices C–F extend the existing structure with analyses and a data-flow explanation; the main sections and earlier appendices are substantially retained.

P2.justification: Figures 15 and 17 visualize new comparisons, Figure 16 diagrams existing loss computations, and Table 8 is added. Figure 12 becomes a paired distribution plot and drops the original printed category percentages. Several retained figures are resized or repositioned, including Figure 8 moving from page 11 to page 10.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for the paper through a direct fine-tuning comparison, evaluation of the original PHC controller, and a check of the auxiliary forward-dynamics model against Nimble. The expanded data-flow explanation also improves clarity. These are useful, limited gains: transfer evidence remains a qualitative knee example, and Table 8 provides little evaluation detail, so the additions do not establish a substantial overall quality improvement.
